newsitem.title: USA: Hercules muscles into crowded corp debt arena.
newsitem.headline: Hercules muscles into crowded corp debt arena.

text.p: Hercules Inc is expected to muscle in among other opportunistic issuers looking to capitalize on lower rates to finance debt, as anxious investors clamor for more, dealers said.
"Market tone remains very good and supply has been easily absorbed," said one syndicate source. "I imagine we'll have another busy week."
Currently, the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond remains below 6.50 percent, drawing more issuers into the market.
Among them is Hercules' $200 million debt offering.

The Delaware-based, global producer of chemicals and related products is expected to issue a two-part deal consisting of $100 million three-year notes and $100 million 30-year debt with a put option, players said.
The offering is expected to be underwritten by JP Morgan Securities and NationsBanc Capital Markets, they said.
Among other high-grade offerings is Brunswick Corp's $200 million Baa1/BBB-plus rated 30-year debt via Merrill Lynch & Co. The deal has a Treasury make-whole call, dealers said.
Another $150 million in 30-year debt, putable in seven-years, will come from Quebecor Printing.
